document.title: Letter of Filippo Bruni and note concerning a manuscript attributed to Cecco d'Ascoli
document.catalog_description: Lettera di Filippo Bruni con notizie su un manoscritto con un inedito di Cecco di Ascoli

transcriptions.text: Questa opera però, detta l'Acerba, è stampata. La presente mai si è veduta; il metro lo stesso, il carattere, la carta la provano di Cecco.
This work, however, called L'Acerba, is printed. The present one has never been seen; the same meter, the script, and the paper prove it to be by Cecco.
unclear_spans: The referent of 'la presente' requires expert confirmation.

claims.statement: The 1745 note explicitly distinguishes printed L'Acerba from the manuscript then under discussion.

evidence.description: The note says L'Acerba is printed and then says 'la presente mai si è veduta.'
The immediately preceding quoted verses match the known text of L'Acerba.

alternatives: The phrase 'la presente' may refer to a particular witness or version of L'Acerba rather than a separate work.
claims.falsification_test: Independent transcription and syntactic analysis of ff. 117r-117v.
claims.novelty_search: Initial exact-phrase, shelfmark, author, catalog, and manuscript-census searches completed on 2026-07-26; no scholarly discussion of this specific claim located.

claims.statement: A manuscript presented in 1745 as an unpublished and separate work of Cecco d'Ascoli may be lost, dispersed, or cataloged under another identity.

evidence.description: Bruni appears to send or arrange inspection of a physical manuscript.
The enclosed note calls the item unpublished and distinguishes it from printed L'Acerba.

evidence.locator: Catalogo della Libreria Capponi (1747), manuscript appendix
evidence.description: No searchable Cecco, Acerba, or Ascoli entry was found.

alternatives: The object was an ordinary or unusual L'Acerba witness.
The attribution and antiquity were eighteenth-century errors.
The manuscript was returned to its owner and survives elsewhere.
The manuscript is in the Vatican or another collection under an unidentified title.
claims.falsification_test: Locate the object or a fuller description and compare its text against the L'Acerba tradition and Cecco's authenticated works.
claims.novelty_search: Initial web, Vatican catalog, Capponi 1747 catalog, Cozzo 1897 catalog, and general Cecco bibliography searches completed; specialist databases and critical-edition review remain.
